paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar or Rabbi Yose ben Delagai. Yoma 39b and Tamid 30b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The source gives the alternatives Rabbi Elazar or Rabbi Yose ben Delagai; it does not separately repeat the patronymic after Elazar. Both alternatives are retained.

The William Davidson digital text of Yoma 39b has Rabbi (Yose ben) Dulgai, while Tamid 30b has Rabbi Elazar ben Diglai. Hyman’s Delagai spelling, alternatives, and patronymic scope are retained; these local title attestations do not harmonize the names or establish that the two reports concern one person.
